scope: UI-only Firefox diagnostics regression; no live anonymity, proof-verification or wallet-transaction claim.

setup.server: Dedicated temporary Vite development server and cache fixture on ephemeral loopback ports; no existing server or environment files used.
setup.privateWindow: Fresh profile launched with --private-window; autostart false, PrivateBrowsingUtils window and selected-browser flags asserted true. Normal profile flags asserted false. Headless Firefox.
setup.transport: Dedicated Vite transform replaces only anon-transport.ts in memory with a rejected stub; every page asserts Transport disabled for UI QA. The actual worker/KPS/WebRTC transport does not start in these cases.
setup.independentNetworkLog: Firefox chrome-context nsIHttpChannel observer for this owned Firefox process: http-on-modify-request, http-on-examine-response, http-on-examine-cached-response. Independent of ResourceTiming. Tab attribution recorded when Firefox exposes a matching browsing context; missing subresource attribution is not filtered away. Local fixture server hits separately counted.
setup.sanitization: HTTP URLs contain origin labels and paths only: no query, fragment or workspace absolute path. External origins/paths redacted. No headers, bodies, tokens, profile paths or user data collected.
setup.timingsUnavailable: Additional private-window cases shadow PerformanceObserver and performance.getEntriesByType before app startup. This is a deliberate compatibility simulation, not Firefox's default private behavior.

limitations: Development pages with explicit transport stub; does not replace live/public gateway, release-build, Tor exit or verified-read checks.

HTTP-channel log is bounded and scoped to the owned Firefox process. Background HTTP may be included; tab attribution is incomplete for subresources. WebRTC, non-HTTP transports and full OS network activity are not measured.
ResourceTiming entries measure exposed observations, not all connections. Clearing the browser buffer must not erase previously retained rows; collection remains bounded to 512 observations per page.
Cache fixture is a local HTTP resource; private caching is tested within one private-window lifetime, not persistence after closing private browsing.
